My scratch probes are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/` (`handed.mjs`, `gest.mjs`). ## 0. Test run (from repo root, absolute paths) `node --test /home/user/threadgame/kit/connected/Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit/code/touch-input.test.mjs /home/user/threadgame/kit/connected/Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit/code/route-motion.test.mjs` on Node v22.22.0: ``` 1..34 # tests 34 # suites 0 # pass 34 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0 ``` This matches the kit's own record in `docs/VERIFICATION.json:5-7`. The split is 26 touch-input tests and 8 route-motion tests. ## 1. Public API and behaviour ### touch-input.mjs (browser ES module, no dependencies) **Constants** - `DEFAULTS` (`touch-input.mjs:2-6`): ```js { swipeWidthRatio: 0.08, swipeMin: 24, swipeMax: 72, axisDominance: 1.2, tapSlop: 10, tapDuration: 200, doubleTapInterval: 320, doubleTapDistance: 24 } ``` - `INTENTS` (`:8-14`), all frozen: - `left` = `{type:'steer',direction:-1}` - `right` = `{type:'steer',direction:1}` - `jump` = `{type:'jump'}` - `togglePlayerBrake` = `{type:'toggle-player-brake'}` - `toggleGlobalPause` = `{type:'toggle-global-pause'}` (only a button emits this, never a gesture) **Swipe threshold** `swipeThreshold(w)` (`:16-20`): `clamp(0.08*w, 24, 72)` CSS px. An invalid or zero width falls back to 320, giving 25.6. Measured: 32.96 px at 412 wide, 28.8 px at 360 wide. The current game uses 36 px (`game/src/ui/input.js:30`). **Classifier** `classifyGesture({dx,dy,duration,maxDistance,viewportWidth})` (`:23-32`): - **tap**: `duration ≤ 200` and `max(maxDistance, |d|) ≤ 10` (`:26`). - **left/right**: `|dx| ≥ thr` and `|dx| ≥ 1.2|dy|` (`:29`). - **jump** (up) or **reserved** (down): the same test on the vertical axis (`:30`). - **none**: everything else. - It uses the net displacement at release. `maxDistance` only matters for the tap test, so a drag-return gives `none`. **Gesture machine** `createGestureMachine(opts)` (`:38-107`) has no DOM dependency. Each method returns `[]` or `[intent]`. - **Clock**: time must be a finite monotonic number. Non-finite throws `TypeError`; a backwards step is clamped (`:42-46`). - **`down`** (`:54-67`): - A duplicate pointer id is a no-op. - `ignored:true` or a second contact clears the stroke and the pending tap and sets `blocked`. - **`move`** (`:68-70`) only updates the position and `maxDistance`. It never emits anything. - **`up`** (`:71-94`): this is the only point where a stroke resolves, once. - **Double tap**: the second tap's release is within 320 ms of the first tap's release, and its start is within 24 px of the first tap's start (`:84-85`). A single tap does nothing. After a pair, a third tap starts a new pair (`:86`). - Any non-tap result, including `none` and `reserved`, clears the pending tap (`:92`). - `blocked` clears only when every tracked pointer has lifted (`:78`). - **`cancel(id,{retainPointer})`** (`:95-101`): clears the stroke and the pending tap. With `retainPointer`, the pointer stays tracked, so the machine stays blocked until that pointer actually goes up. - **`reset()`** (`:102-105`): clears everything. **DOM adapter** `attachTouchInput(surface, onIntent, opts)` (`:112-158`) returns `{reset, dispose}`. - **Listeners**: on `document`, capture phase, `passive:false` (`:119-122`). - **UI exclusion**: selector `'[data-ui],button,a,input,select,textarea,[contenteditable="true"],[role="button"]'`, checked against the composed path and `closest` (`:116-117,128`). - **A down is ignored when** (`:131-132`): - it starts outside the surface, or - it starts on UI, or - `button !== 0`, or - it is a non-primary touch. This guards a second finger that arrives after a `reset()`. - **Accepted downs**: `preventDefault` and `setPointerCapture` (`:134-137`). - **Moves**: coalesced events are replayed (`:139-144`). - **Cancellation**: - `pointercancel` → `cancel(id)` (`:148`). - `lostpointercapture` → `cancel(id,{retainPointer:true})` (`:151`). This is harmless after a normal `pointerup` because the id is already gone (test `:120-129`). - **Lifecycle**: window `blur` and a hidden `visibilitychange` call `reset()` (`:152-153`). `dispose()` removes every listener and resets (`:156`). - **Time source**: `opts.now` overrides it (default `performance.now`, `:115`). ### route-motion.mjs **`sampleRoad(route, distance, lateral=0, bodyRadius=0.35)`** (`:6-23`) - Validates its inputs and throws `TypeError` on bad ones (`:8`). It also throws if `s` does not strictly increase (`:13`). - Clamps `s` to `[first.s, last.s]` (`:9`), then finds the segment by binary search (`:10-11`). - Interpolates the centre linearly. `forward` is the normalised lerp of the two tangents (`:16`). - `right = unit([f.z, 0, -f.x])` (`:17`) and `normal = f × right` (`:18`). There is no bank. - `width` uses each point's width or falls back to `route.width` (`:19`). - **Lateral clamp**: `limit = max(0, width/2 - bodyRadius)` (`:20-21`). That is ±2.65 m on main (width 6) and ±0.95 m on the branch (width 2.6). - Returns `{s, center, position, forward, right, normal, width, lateral, heading: atan2(f.x,f.z), mainS}`. - `mainS` is the lerp of the points' `mainS` on a branch, and `s` itself on main, whose points have no `mainS` (`:22`). **`advanceRun(state{s,speed,phase,braked}, dt, {runSpeed, accelerationTime=0.3, brakingTime=0.22, strideLength=1.4, paused=false, routeLength=Infinity})`** (`:25-38`) - Exact constant-acceleration integration within a step: speed changes for part of `dt`, then cruises (`:30-35`). - Acceleration is `runSpeed/accelerationTime`; deceleration is `runSpeed/brakingTime`. - `paused` or `dt===0` returns the state unchanged with `distanceMoved:0` (`:29`). - At `routeLength` the runner clamps, speed becomes 0 and the overshoot is dropped (`:36-37`). - `phase = frac(phase + d/strideLength)`, so the stride is driven by distance. **`chaseTargets(route, distance, lateral, {behind=5.5, height=3.2, lookAhead=7, targetHeight=0.8})`** (`:40-46`) - Camera position = player position − forward·5.5 + 3.2 Y. Look target = the road sample at `s+7` (same lateral) + 0.8 Y. - No smoothing and no collision. **Branches**: there is no graph code. The only branch support is `sampleRoad(branchObj, localS)` plus the `mainS` field. `ROUTE-MOTION.txt:16` tells the host to switch from main `s` to branch `s` at the fork, back to main `endS` at the rejoin, and to use `mainS` for race progress. ## 2. Fork position: branch lateral is 0 at branch s=0, 1.24 m at s=3, 2.6 m at s=5, 5.0 m max at s≈10. Its width (2.6) also tightens the lateral clamp from ±2.65 to ±0.95, so switching "at the exact connection" from a main lateral of +2.65 snaps the runner by up to 1.7 m. A world-space or projection-based handoff is needed; the kit has no `project()`. | | **"Valid shorter route"** (prompt:24) | — | The only branch is longer: 19.543 m against 15.986 m of main, about 0.7 s slower at 5 m/s. A shortcut needs new data or a different reason to take the branch. | | **Jump physics** | none (`ROUTE-MOTION.txt:3`) | Keep the existing sim: `jumpTime 0.68`, `sin(πt)`, `inputBufferTime 0.15`, `jumpAirborneAbove 0.3` (`core/ww.js:19-21`, `sim/race.js:576-580`). The fork and rejoin decks overlap, and the kit says to bake a collision union. The host must drop intents while paused (`README.md:37`) and call `reset()` when the pause screen or a mode changes (`README:24`). This fits the current lifecycle (`ARCHITECTURE.md §9`). | | **Determinism / fixed 1/60 step** | `advanceRun` is pure (verified) | At 1/60: braking from 4 m/s covers 0.43999999999999984 m (exact answer 0.44); 0→4 m/s takes 18 steps and 0.600000 m; two replays of a 6000-step run with brake toggling were identical. The gesture machine runs on wall-clock `performance.now()` but stays on the input side, so the sim remains deterministic for a given intent sequence. Intents must still be queued into `race.input()` between steps, as now. No RNG is involved. | | **Swipe latency** | resolves on release only (`README:20`, `:68-70`) | A 300 ms swipe fires at 300 ms. That also clears pending taps and blocks other gestures until the finger lifts. 3. Keep the sim-side guard `if (st.tutorial) return;` (`race.js:570`) and extend it to brake toggles. 4. Call `reset()` when the lesson hold starts and ends. 5. Never mount both adapters on the canvas (`README:75`). **Edge cases I verified** - **Handedness (most important).** `right = [f.z,0,-f.x]` is +X when facing +Z. glTF is right-handed with −X as right. I projected `sampleRoad(s, ±1)` through three r147 (`game/vendor/three.min.js`) with a `PerspectiveCamera` aimed with `chaseTargets`. At s = 5, 40, 81, 120 and 180, **lateral +1 lands on the screen's left** (for example, at s=5 the NDC x is −0.897 against +0.722 for lateral −1). - The data uses the same convention (`generate_course.py:47`; `scenery/README.md:17` calls it "right"). Collectible positions reproduce exactly with it (error 0.0000 with +Y hover). - So the data is consistent, but `INTENTS.right` (+1) must map to lateral −1 in a three.js render. Alternatively, negate the vector in one place. - The branch sits at kit lateral +0…+5, so on screen it is to the **left** of the main road. - **Look-ahead clamps at a route's end** (`:42-43`, via `:9`). At the branch end, the target stops at the branch end instead of continuing onto main. At the finish, the target is directly above Purl (horizontal distance 0), so the camera looks straight down. The look-ahead has to sample across the route graph and past the finish. - `chaseTargets` re-clamps lateral with `bodyRadius` 0.35, whatever the host uses. - The camera's "behind" offset follows the current tangent, not the road. It strays at most 0.64 m (horizontal) from the centreline on this layout. - **Branch overshoot.** With `routeLength` set to the branch length, `advanceRun` sets speed to 0 and loses the leftover distance (0.0234 m in one 1/60 step). For handoff, pass `Infinity` and convert `s − branch.length + endS` yourself. - **Capture loss without a `pointerup`.** The machine stays blocked until that pointer lifts or `reset()` is called (verified). This is intended, but the host must call `reset()` on mode changes. - **Taps.** A tap must be ≤200 ms, against the current game's 300 ms (`input.js:29`). A 201 ms touch counts as `none` and cancels a pending double tap. This needs device tuning. ## 3. Integration recommendation: classic scripts on `WW`, not ES modules **Why** - `ARCHITECTURE.md §1-2` requires classic scripts on `globalThis.WW` that also open from `file://`. - `tests/unit/load.cjs:20-33` loads `src/(core|data|sim)` scripts from `index.html` with `vm.runInThisContext`, which cannot evaluate ES modules. - ES modules would load in the WebView: the androidx.webkit 1.14.0 `MimeUtil` maps both `js` and `mjs` to `text/javascript` (checked with `javap`, switch cases 33 and 34 → offset 1506). They would still fail from `file://` (kit `README.md:3`) and in the Node sim tests. - House style: `game/src` has no arrow functions, `?.`, `??`, `.at(`, or `catch {}` (grep found 0). The kit uses all of them. **Port with the logic unchanged (syntax only)** - `game/src/core/gesture.js` → `WW.gesture = {DEFAULTS, INTENTS, swipeThreshold, classify, createMachine}`, with all of `touch-input.mjs:2-107`. Putting it in `core` lets `load.cjs` test it in Node. - `game/src/ui/touch.js` → `WW.ui.attachTouch`, porting `:112-158`: capture-phase document listeners, coalesced moves, capture loss with the pointer retained, blur/visibility reset, the `isPrimary` guard and the UI selector. Add: - the pull-target start hook; - an optional `tap{x,y}` intent; - the keyboard handling from `input.js:174-200`. This replaces the pointer half of `createInput`. Keep `cancelPull`/`active` for `main.js:191,213`. - `game/src/core/route.js` → `WW.route = {sample, advance, chase}`, with `sampleRoad` and `advanceRun` as written and `chaseTargets` only as a starting point. **Rewrite** - Fix the lateral sign: either the right vector or the intent mapping. - Add a route-graph wrapper: racer `{routeId, s, lateral, braked, …}`, progress as `mainS`, fork/rejoin handoff with lateral blending, overflow carry, and a junction window with side selection. - Look-ahead that crosses the graph, plus time-based camera damping in the renderer (not the sim). - Brake, jump and the Snagling contact in `sim/race.js`. - Loop AI re-targeted onto the route. - Convert `route.json` into a script (`game/src/data/route.js`, `WW.ROUTE = …`, 135 KB), because `fetch` of JSON fails under `file://` and `load.cjs` only runs JS. - Port the kit's 34 tests into `tests/unit/*.test.cjs` through `load()`, and add tests for the pull/tap/brake interactions. ## 4. ## 1. World representation (current engine)

- **Coordinates.** All gameplay geometry is in plate pixels (841×1870), one painted image per plate (`game/src/core/ww.js:8`, `game/src/render/camera.js:14`, `game/src/render/renderer.js:17`). A racer has no world position. Its state is `{seg, f, laneX, jumpH}` (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:45-55).
- **Plate segments.** Each plate has its own `purl.path` and `loop.path` as `[x, y, w, lane]` control points in plate px. `w` is the sprite width at that point, so depth scale is authored by hand. `lane` is a horizontal pixel offset between lanes (`core/path.js:3-10`).
  - The path is a Catmull-Rom spline. `f` is measured in racer widths: `len = |dp| / w` (`path.js:46-47`).
  - Lanes are a screen-horizontal shift `x + laneX*lane`; a jump lifts the sprite by `jumpH*0.42*w` (`path.js:93-97`). Lanes do not follow the heading.
  - Purl and Loop run on different painted paths on every plate (e.g. `data/plates/p01.js:9-12` vs `:23`). They never share a road.
- **Events are plate fractions.** Stops, pickups, reveal, exit, finish and Loop tasks are `f` values, some with plate-px `x, y` (`p01.js:14-27`, `p04.js:23-24`, `p07.js:21,38`). `parseRoute` reads them into each segment (`sim/race.js:45-85`).
- **Level route** (`data/level.js:38-60`) alternates six `plate` segments with five `connector` segments of 19 m each. `loopRoute` is index-aligned with Loop's own lengths (`level.js:63-73`), and `race.js:149-155` enforces that alignment.
  - A racer advances `df = v·dt/length` (`level.js:8`).
  - Purl's route to the finish is about 445.7 m. The five connectors make up 95 m of it (21%) and 19 s of a roughly 98 s race.
- **What a connector is.** A segment with only `length`, `from`, `to` and `style`. `parseRoute` gives plates a path (`race.js:54-57`) but leaves a connector's `path: null` (`race.js:50`, accepted at `:78`). It has no events, no lanes in plate data and no geometry.
  - Entering one sets `state.transition = {kind:'connector', t: f, dur: length/purlSpeed}` (`race.js:376-386`). Each step copies `t = p.f` (`race.js:485`) and sets Purl's action to `'transition'` (`race.js:515`).
  - Loop's action on a connector is also `'transition'` (`sim/loop-ai.js:270`).
  - **No floor geometry exists for any connector, in the sim or the renderer.** The sim even allows lane swipes there, using a made-up spacing of `connectorLaneSpacing: 100` (`race.js:34, 346-349`), which the renderer ignores.

## 2. Root cause of the 0:36–0:37 "blurred pillar wipe"

**Sim side**
- When Purl walks from `ribbon` into `c-ribbon`, `enterPurl` calls `setTransitionFor` (`race.js:388-399`). From then on, `transition.t` is just Purl's progress `f` through the empty 19 m segment.

**Renderer side**
- `resolveScene` turns a connector segment into `{kind:'transition', from:'p01', to:'p02', t}` (`renderer.js:58-65`). `render` then calls `drawTransitionScene` (`renderer.js:580-582`). That function:
  1. Freezes a snapshot of the outgoing camera and Purl's last screen pose (`renderer.js:406-415`).
  2. Builds two flat 2D plate views, slid ±0.32·W horizontally: p01 out, p02 in (`renderer.js:418-421`).
  3. Draws each view clipped to the rectangle on either side of a sweeping x, with racers off (`purl:false`) (`renderer.js:425-430`).
  4. Draws the "tower column" with `drawColumn` (`renderer.js:432, 474-494`). The column is the outgoing plate's `wipe` strip (`p01.js:37`, `{x0:345, x1:560}`), blurred with `blur(2.5px)` and darkened (`columnCanvas`, `renderer.js:454-472`, blur at `:463`), scaled 1.12×, full screen height (`columnGeom`, `renderer.js:445-451`), with fake contact shadows.
  5. Draws Purl in screen space, after everything else, at a straight interpolation between the p01-exit pose and the p02-entry pose (`renderer.js:434-440`). There is no ground under him. He is drawn on top of the blurred column.
  6. Hard-sets the camera to the p02 entry (`renderer.js:441`).
- Loop is drawn only when he is on a `plate` segment (`renderer.js:316-319`), so he disappears during his own connector.
- The same code runs for the `loop` (recovery) and `return` (gate fallback) transitions (`renderer.js:51-56`; sim `race.js:419-433`).

**Measured in the real game** (Playwright, 412×915, seed 1; script `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/capture.cjs`, frame `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/connector-t0.5.png`)
- At t = 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, Purl's screen (x, y, w) is (208, 524, 84) → (188, 651, 115) → (168, 778, 146).
- The views are p01 at s = 0.881 (zoom 1.8, the `zMax` from `p01.js:6`) and p02 at s = 0.489 (zoom 1).
- So Purl shrinks to 84 px at the far end of each plate, then snaps back to the foreground at about 146 px. Cause: zoom `z = clamp(w0/w, 1, zMax)` (`camera.js:47-62`) plus the camera snapping when the plate changes (`renderer.js:392`).
- Loop was on `ribbon` at t = 0.1 (drawn in the p01 strip) and on `c-ribbon` at t = 0.5 (not drawn).
- The frame shows the blurred pillar with Purl floating over it.

**Timing check** (headless sim, `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/timing.cjs`, real `race.step`)

| Moment | Wall clock after START | Race clock |
|---|---|---|
| Countdown ends (3 s, `ww.js:15`) | 3.0 s | 0 s |
| Purl at the ribbon stop; lesson hold begins | 3.58 s | 0.57 s |
| Lesson finishes (pull after L s, + 1.3 s unfurl + 0.25 s settle, `ww.js:35,42`) | 7.15 s (L = 2) | 0.57 s (frozen) |
| `c-ribbon` entered | 32.87 s | 26.28 s |
| Column crosses screen centre (t = 0.5) | 34.8 s | — |
| `c-ribbon` ends | 36.67 s | 30.08 s |

- Purl runs 127.2 m at `purlSpeed` 5 m/s (`ww.js:16`) to reach `c-ribbon`.
- In general, the column crosses mid-screen at about 32.8 s + L + (time on the start screen before START).
- So 0:36–0:37 matches **`c-ribbon` (p01→p02)** if the lesson reaction plus start-screen dwell is about 3–4 s. This is consistent but not confirmed: recording 6746.mp4 is not in the repo.
- Later connectors (L = 2) fall at about 50–54, 70–74, 81–85 and 98–101 s after START, which matches "similar transitions recur later".

**Side defect seen in the same frame.** The HUD reads PURL 1/3 but the objective still says "Collect the coral thread". `inventory.collect` never calls `refreshObjective` (`sim/inventory.js:61-69`), and `refreshObjective` returns early on connectors (`race.js:404`). The kit asks for objectives to update immediately.

## 3. Can the current renderer do connected geometry with a turning chase camera?

**Structurally impossible in this pipeline:**
- **The camera cannot turn.** It has three degrees of freedom `{plate, z, fx, fy}`. A view is a uniform scale plus translate `{s, ox, oy}`, applied with one `setTransform` (`camera.js:81-84`, `renderer.js:152`), and it is clamped inside one plate (`camera.js:64-70`). There is no yaw, pitch or perspective.
- **The world is one fixed-viewpoint painting per plate**, cut from a rectangle with `drawImage` (`render/world.js` `drawPlate`). The camera can't follow a bend: rotating a painting does not reveal a new heading, and the painting has no unseen sides.
- **Depth is hard-coded for one view.** Depth is sort-by-ground-y in plate px (`renderer.js:324`). Occlusion is hand-drawn 2D polygons with a `behindY` line that redraw plate pixels (`renderer.js:325-333`; `p01.js:31-36`). Racer depth scale is the authored `w` per control point. All of this is valid only for the fixed viewpoint.
- **Lanes are screen-horizontal** (`path.js:96`), not perpendicular to the heading.
- **The canvas holds a 2D context** (`renderer.js:24`), so the same `<canvas id="view">` cannot also give a WebGL context. A 3D view needs a new canvas, or the 2D renderer replaced on that element.
- Canvas 2D could in theory software-rasterise a flat-shaded blockout (painter's sort, affine-only textures, no z-buffer). That would be a new renderer, not an extension, with poor mobile quality and performance.

**Merely missing (can sit on a new 3D renderer):**
- **Directional character views.** Only rear frames exist: 8 poses each for purl/loop (`asset-data.js`; `actors.js:4-7` "Front poses … never used"). `purlFront`/`loopFront` `f1..f8` are used only for portraits. There are no side or three-quarter views for a turning camera.
- **A better run cycle.** It is 4 frames per 1.6 m (`actors.js:13-14, 28-31`). The kit asks for contact / push-off / swing / landing.
- **Projecting 3D foot points to screen** for sprites. Sprites already use foot pivots (`render/util.js:36-42` uses `fr.px/py`; `actors.scaleFor`, `actors.js:21`), so they can be drawn as billboards or as a 2D overlay at projected anchors.
- **A camera rig, depth-tested occlusion, and a WebGL library.** `game/vendor/three.min.js` (three r147 UMD) appeared during this inspection (autosave `4c38eb2`, 18:42:58Z). It is not referenced by `game/index.html` (scripts at lines 188-224) and contains no GLTFLoader (grep count 0).

## 4. Reuse table

**Core and data**

| Module | Verdict | Reason / plate–pixel assumptions |
|---|---|---|
| `core/ww.js` | KEEP WITH CHANGES | `rng`, `util`, timing tuning are generic. ## 5. Android host

- **Hardware acceleration is on.** `android:hardwareAccelerated="true"` (`AndroidManifest.xml:12`). The WebView is created programmatically with no `setLayerType(SOFTWARE)` (`MainActivity.java:153-223`). Nothing in the host blocks WebGL; availability depends on the device's WebView GPU support.
- Backgrounding calls `web.onPause()` / `pauseTimers()` (`MainActivity.java:308-316`). A WebGL renderer should handle `webglcontextlost` / `webglcontextrestored`. A renderer crash is recovered by `onRenderProcessGone` (`MainActivity.java:206-210`).
- **No CSP.** There is no `<meta http-equiv>` in `game/index.html:3-11`, and no headers are added by the asset loader.
- **The host is local-only.**
  - There is no INTERNET permission (`AndroidManifest.xml:3-4`).
  - Every URL outside `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/assets/` gets a 403, and missing files get a 404 (`MainActivity.java:189-197, 247-255`).
  - So three.js, loaders and decoders must ship inside `game/`; a CDN won't work.
  - The build script's own comment says external/data URLs are blocked (`build-android.sh:124`). Use `.glb`, not `.gltf` with base64 data-URI buffers. three.js turns embedded GLB images into `blob:` URLs, which the host doesn't intercept; verify on device.
- **MIME types** (from `androidx.webkit` 1.14.0 `MimeUtil.class` in the gradle cache; dependency at `build.gradle:72`):
  - `js`/`mjs` are served as `text/javascript`, `json` as `application/json`, `wasm` as `application/wasm`.
  - `glb`/`gltf`/`bin` are not in the table, so they fall back to `URLConnection` guessing and then `text/plain`. That is harmless for `fetch().arrayBuffer()` / XHR arraybuffer.
- **Packaging.**
  - `bundleGame` syncs only `../game` (`build.gradle:78-91`), excluding `*.md` and `tests/`. Kit files under `kit/connected/...` (e.g. `scenery/*.glb`, `route.json`) must be copied into `game/`.
  - `noCompress` lacks `glb` (`build.gradle:59-61`). That works, it is just deflated.
  - `build-android.sh:90` runs `assembleDebug`, and `preBuild` depends on `bundleGame` (`build.gradle:104`).
- `file://` opening of `index.html` (ARCHITECTURE §1) cannot `fetch` a `.glb`. That property is lost unless the geometry is embedded as a JS data script.
- Insets are applied as root padding and consumed, so `env()` reads 0 in the app (`MainActivity.java:123-149`, `style.css:43-48`). This can stay.

## Recommended reuse plan

1. **Keep the sim's rule core** and give it a metres-based route instead of plate fractions: inventory, stitches (including the pull lesson and tutorial hold), Snagling rules, Loop's seeded plan, finish/ranks/gate check, pause/determinism and the debug API. Replace `seg`/`f`/`laneX` with route `s` in metres (main road plus branch id), lateral offset in metres within the road width, and heading taken from the route tangent. Port the kit's route math into a classic `WW.*` script and convert `route.json` into a `game/src/data/*.js` data file, so `tests/unit/load.cjs` and the Android verify step see it.
2. **Delete the connector concept.** That covers `kind: 'connector'`, `setTransitionFor`, `transition.kind === 'connector'`, `connectorLaneSpacing`, `wipe`, `columnGeom`/`columnCanvas`/`drawColumn` and `drawTransitionScene`. Redesign the recovery loop and the gate "return" as physical behaviour on the connected road (e.g. drop the thread ahead on the road, or a visible turnaround) rather than a wipe that moves Purl.
3. **Put Purl and Loop on the same road** with separate lateral positions. Turn Loop's `bypass` into a real branch traversal, add steering/branch choice for Purl, and add the double-tap brake toggle as a new `race.input` type that does not pause Loop. Re-measure pacing and rewrite `level.pacing` and `pacing.test.cjs`.
4. **Write a new 3D world renderer behind the same public API** (`resize`/`render`/`handleEvents`/`getTapTargets`/`getLayout`; new `worldToScreen`). Use a separate WebGL canvas and the vendored three.js, which still needs a local GLTF loader; no CDN in the APK. Load the kit's GLB blockout from `game/` through an extended `ui/loader.js`, with a chase camera that turns with the route. Draw characters, spools, Snagling, cues and fx at projected foot anchors, using the existing atlas frames and pivots as an interim. Report the rear-only/directional-view gap and the 4-frame gait as asset/animation gaps.
5. **Reuse the 2D layers as an overlay:** `actors.drawRacer` / `drawSpool`, `util`, `fx` (screen-space parts), `features.drawCue`, the `pull.js` lesson poses and prompts (re-anchored to the 3D stitch), and `setpieces.afterRacer` effects. Re-author tassels, butterfly, gate and Snagling positions in route/world coordinates.
6. **Keep the UI stack as is:** HUD, overlays, dom layout, main loop, lifecycle, test API, locked cash-out. Add Left/Right/Jump/Run-Stop buttons and the double-tap brake in `input.js`/`index.html`/`style.css`. Fix the objective refresh on pickup. Update the help copy.
7. **Android:** no host changes are needed for WebGL. Copy the GLB and route data into `game/`, optionally add `glb` to `noCompress`, extend the verify step in `build-android.sh` to check the new files, and handle WebGL context loss.
8. **Tests:** keep `tests/unit` rule coverage, retargeted to route `s` and the new ids. Replace `tests/e2e/opening.cjs` (which asserts the wipe at `:39`) with an uninterrupted connected-opening scenario. Keep `tests/e2e/lib.cjs`. Retire the plate-specific `tests/harness/*`.
